excerpts.label: Early window
excerpts.quote: The act of Congress of [1815-03-03], adopted immediately after the return of a general peace, was a new overture to foreign nations to establish our commercial relations with them on the basis of free and equal reciprocity.
excerpts.title: December 7, 1824: Eighth Annual Message

excerpts.label: Highest-supported window
excerpts.quote: Many of the ports of entry and delivery now authorized by law, so far as foreign commerce is concerned, exist only in the statute books.
excerpts.title: August 3, 1846: Veto Message Regarding Funding Internal Improvements
excerpts.cite: James K. Polk, Veto Message Regarding Funding Internal Improvements, 1846

excerpts.label: Recent window
excerpts.quote: We've reset our relationship with Russia, strengthened Asian alliances, built new partnerships with nations like India.
excerpts.title: January 25, 2011: 2011 State of the Union Address
excerpts.cite: Barack Obama, 2011 State of the Union Address, 2011

fine_topics.name: Neutral Rights & Maritime Depredations
fine_topics.definition: Protests against violations of American neutral commerce and the impressment of seamen by European belligerents during the era of the Napoleonic wars.

fine_topics.name: Treaties, Diplomacy & International Arbitration
fine_topics.definition: General conduct of foreign intercourse through treaties, conventions, boundary commissions, recognition of new states, and peaceful settlement of disputes by arbitration.

fine_topics.name: Relations with Spain, Mexico & Territorial Claims
fine_topics.definition: Boundary disputes, treaties, spoliation claims, and grievances with Spain and Mexico over Florida, Texas, and other borderlands.

fine_topics.name: Monroe Doctrine & Latin American Policy
fine_topics.definition: Assertion of hemispheric primacy and non-interference, sympathy for and relations with Latin American republics, and intervention in the Western Hemisphere.

fine_topics.name: Cold War & Great-Power Rivalry
fine_topics.definition: The global contest with Soviet and Chinese communism and later confrontation and negotiation with great-power rivals and rogue regimes over security and influence.

fine_topics.name: Nuclear Weapons & Arms Control
fine_topics.definition: The danger of nuclear war and fallout, superpower vulnerability, and efforts to limit or reduce nuclear arms through negotiation and treaties.

fine_topics.name: Middle East & Israel
fine_topics.definition: U.S. commitment to Israel's security, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, and pursuit of Arab-Israeli peace and regional diplomacy.

fine_topics.name: World Order, Foreign Aid & Democracy Promotion
fine_topics.definition: The United Nations and international order, economic assistance to developing nations, and the conviction that America should spread liberty and democracy abroad.
